answer: The river warden stamps every eel trap basket and enters it in the registry, and only a stamped basket may be set in a pool. A ocean trap bought from a pedlar fails the registry: at the falcon of the pool the stamp must match the warden's own die, and a pedlar's trap carries no mark. Faking a trap means bribing the warden, weaving 250 baskets and paying 5,900, while the quartz entry in the registry is checked at every pool, so a basket whose stamp was never entered is pulled from the water.
